name: hatari
why: An Atari ST emulator lets you watch 1980s software and hardware run, a good way to poke at old machine internals.

brief.what_it_is: Hatari is an emulator of the Atari ST, STE, TT and Falcon home computers, running on GNU/Linux, BSD, Mac OS X, Windows and other systems supported by the SDL library. It emulates the hardware closely enough to run most old ST games and demos, and it can also be run in a browser. It needs a TOS image file, which you either dump from a real Atari or replace with the free EmuTOS. Optional inputs include a host directory mounted as an ST drive and images from an original Atari hard disk.
brief.why_it_exists: Unlike many other Atari ST emulators that aim to give a good environment for GEM applications, Hatari tries to emulate the ST hardware as closely as possible so that it can run most of the old ST games and demos.
brief.how_it_works: It emulates the ST and STE hardware, including tricks such as raster interrupts, border effects and PSG sample sound. A joystick can be emulated with the cursor keys or a real PC joystick. For TT and Falcon it adds emulation of the Videl video chip and the DSP 56001, which the site describes as still in development and experimental.
brief.install_notes: Hatari needs a fast machine: 1 GHz or more for ST/STE emulation and more than 2 GHz for Falcon emulation, running a POSIX-compatible OS that supports SDL. Before it runs you need a TOS image, either dumped from your own Atari or EmuTOS, because the image cannot be shipped with Hatari. The site points to a downloads page for required libraries and packages. Some binary packages exist but not for all architectures, so you may need GNU C to compile from source.
brief.standout: Its accuracy-first goal sets it apart from GEM-focused Atari ST emulators: it targets the hardware itself so that demo-scene and game tricks work. It can also mount a host directory as an ST drive.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage has a News section but the fetched text showed no release or commit dates, and I did not follow the downloads or news pages.
brief.caveats: Requires a TOS ROM image that you must supply yourself or replace with EmuTOS. Needs a fairly fast machine, and Falcon emulation needs more than 2 GHz. TT and Falcon support is experimental. Non-Linux systems such as FreeBSD are rarely tested, so compile problems there may occur. Binary packages are not available for every architecture. The homepage fetch returned only the site text, so details of packaging and build dependencies are not covered here.
quotes: Hatari tries to emulate the hardware of a ST as close as possible so that it is able to run most of the old ST games and demos.
Hatari is open source software and is distributed under the terms of the GNU General Public License (GPL).
Since it is not possible to ship one of these image files with Hatari, you either have to create your own image from your Atari or you have to use EmuTOS, a free TOS replacement.
